newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 7-Eleven sets IPO, braves bear market.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 7-Eleven sets IPO, braves bear market.

text.p: Philippine Seven Corp, the exclusive local holder of 7-Eleven franchise, on Tuesday said it will push through with its initial public offering (IPO) in September, braving bearish market conditions.
Philipine Seven will be the first company to go public after the peso's de facto devaluation in July jarred Philippine financial and equities market.
In 1984, Philippine Seven opened its first convenience store in the country amid daunting circumstances. Political instability had left the economy in shambles.

"Like in 1984 when the company was able to weather conditions, we are fully confident that we can launch Philippine Seven successfully as well. Besides, the issue is not too big," Senen Matoto, BPI Capital Corp senior vice-president said.
BPI is the lead IPO underwriter.

"We believe it is the appropriate time to go into the market. We have a global network backing us up, solid relationship with suppliers and among others, the management expertise to know what works and what does not in the Philippines," said Philippine Seven chairman Vicente Paterno.
"We are looking forward to interest rates lowering by the end of the month," Paterno said when asked how market conditions could affect the IPO.
The offering of 71.4 million Philippine Seven shares has been set on September 8 to 19 with the listing date on the week of Sept 29, BPI Capital said.
The offer price will be set on Sept 3 with the price ranging from 6.30 pesos to 7.71 pesos a share.
The company also will proceed with earlier plans to issue warrants with attached bonds to former foreign shareholders of its subsidiary Philippine Seven Properties Corp.
The warrants will allow such shareholders to hold Philippine Seven shares should a law allowing foreign ownership in retail business is passed.
BPI Capital vice-president Dennis Sta. Catalina said the 450 million to 550 million pesos coming from the IPO would be used to finance store expansion from the present 116 to 200 next year.
Paterno said the bulk of the Philippine Seven convenience stores are located in Metro Manila but the company plans to expand to major areas nationwide.

"We may go further out next year through franchising to the North and then to the South in Mindanao. Our game plan is that once we've set up our store in Davao, then we will start to service Eastern Indonesia through franchising," Paterno added.
He said Philippine Seven had been given the right of first refusal for the 7-Eleven license for Eastern Indonesia.

By year-end, Paterno said he expected the company to generate 102 million pesos in net income from last year's 75 million. In 1998, the company will post 160 million pesos from 4.4 billion pesos in sales, he added.
